cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Join Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into a secret plan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Will you help me set up Denise's surprise leaving party at seven?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I spent the last one washing glasses.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I'll wash up. Could you get Denise out of the office while I decorate?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She won't leave before I finish her spreadsheet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send it over. I'll finish her spreadsheet; could you take her for coffee and complain about how little I do?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 status claims are detachable from the helpful task-trading that actually recruits B in A5.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 washing burden is answered after A3 irrelevant ban on details; B4 spreadsheet dependency is used clearly by A5.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 establish workload and a real obstacle to distracting Denise, rather than arbitrary hostility.

heightening.evidence: B4 reveals unfinished work, and A5 solves it while suggesting a cover complaint that supports secrecy.

specificity.evidence: A1 identifies a surprise leaving party and time; B4 supplies the specific office obligation.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 cover complaint earns its wit from A volunteering work, whereas A3 prefix interrupts that natural negotiation.

coach2.stated: A1 surprise party needs setup; B2 remembers washing; B4 says Denise will not leave until spreadsheet completion.
coach2.inferred: A5 complaint is deliberate cover, not a factual claim that A is idle.
coach2.missing: No essential office hierarchy is established, but the Drive negotiation needs none.
coach2.firstDefect: A3 authority preface does not determine the helpful tactic continued in A5.

A1-B2.evidence: A1 asks for secret party help; B2 recalls being left washing glasses.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 offers to wash in response to B2, after an unmotivated question restriction.

A3-B4.evidence: A3 proposes taking Denise out; B4 gives the spreadsheet condition for leaving.

B4-A5.evidence: B4 required spreadsheet prompts A5 to finish it and use coffee as cover.
